The JavaScript (`js/`) and Rust (`rust/`) implementations write byte-identical output for every golden translation.\\n\\n```text\\nsource ──parser──▶ source tree ──understanding rules──▶ meta ──type inference──▶ typed meta\\n  ──meaning rules──▶ ──custom layers──▶ ──context rules──▶ ──emitter──▶ target text\\n  ──lowering──▶ stack machine ──▶ NASM / CIL / JVM (Jasmin)\\nNASM / CIL / JVM ──reader──▶ stack machine ──lifting──▶ meta\\ncontrolled natural text ──reader──▶ meta ──writer──▶ controlled natural text\\n```\\n\\n### Requirements gate (test-driven)\\n\\n`docs/case-studies/issue-1/requirements.lino` lists every requirement from the issue and its comments. `docs/case-studies/issue-1/rosetta-coverage.lino` lists the Rosetta Code algorithm types. `scripts/check-requirements.mjs` checks each requirement against the repository; for example, it compares the language lists of both implementations and checks that every task has a golden in every language. It fails CI (`Rust and cross-language translation` job, and `js/tests/requirements.test.js` under Node, Bun and Deno) unless every requirement is **done** or **blocked with a written reason**.\\n\\nThe gate caught real gaps during this work. The Rust implementation was missing 10 languages; that was fixed and the gate now passes.\\n\\n### Web demo\\n\\n![Web demo translating a Python function to Rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-1-35d65b774bf6/docs/screenshots/web-demo.png?raw=true)\\n\\n`examples/universal-app` is a React demo in which any programming or natural language can be translated to any other. You can paste a whole program, one function or one statement. The `web-e2e` job in `.github/workflows/example-app.yml` drives it in Chromium (`examples/universal-app/e2e/translate.e2e.mjs`) and takes the screenshot above.\\n\\n### Fragments: statements, functions or a whole program\\n\\n`translateFragment` / `parseFragment` (JS) and `translate_fragment` / `parse_fragment` (Rust), plus `universal-translator translate --fragment`, accept a statement, one or more functions, or a whole program. Each comes back as the same kind of fragment in the target. A fragment only has to be complete: a function must end with its closing. Otherwise the translator fails with the reason and the line, for example `The fragment is not complete: it ends before its closing (line 2)`. Goldens for every language are in `examples/programs/fragments/translated/` and are checked by `write-fragments.mjs --check`.\\n\\n### CLI, library, HTTP API and Docker\\n\\n- `universal-translator serve` starts an HTTP API (`GET /languages`, `POST /translate`). It reads `--port`/`--host`, then `PORT`/`HOST`, then `.lenv`, through lino-arguments.\\n- `js/src/index.js` (with types) and the `rust/` crate are the libraries.\\n- The `Dockerfile` image runs the CLI and the server. The release workflow builds it and smoke tests the CLI and the HTTP API.\\n\\n### Source layout and best practices\\n\\n- Sources are split into `src/meta` (shared types and trees), `src/formal` (programming languages, Lean, Rocq and machine code) and `src/natural` (human languages, with a reader and a writer), in both `js/` and `rust/`. The `source-layout` check rejects imports that point outwards from the meta layer.\\n- [`docs/case-studies/issue-1/best-practices.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-1-35d65b774bf6/docs/case-studies/issue-1/best-practices.md) maps the associative technology stack, the code architecture principles and all 17 CI/CD best practices to evidence, or gives a reason when one does not apply. `cargo clippy -D warnings` now runs in CI.\\n- **Test coverage is required by CI.** `npm run test:coverage` replaces `npm test` in the Node.js job. It fails below 94% line, 91% branch or 95% function coverage of `js/src` and `bin`; current coverage is 95.4%, 92.1% and 96.5%. The Rust crate runs the same goldens, but CI does not measure its coverage.\\n\\n### Programming languages (32) and machine code\\n\\n| | |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Languages | JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Lua, PHP, C, C++, C#, Java, Go, Rust, Kotlin, Swift, Perl, Dart, Scala, Julia, R, Groovy, Objective-C, Nim, D, Pascal, Fortran, Ada, Visual Basic .NET, Bash, MATLAB/Octave, Zig, **Lean 4, Rocq** |\\n| Dialects | Pascal, Fortran, Ada, VB.NET, Bash, MATLAB/Octave and Zig have their own program layout. They are dialects of the shared parser and emitter (`js/src/formal/dialects/`, `rust/src/formal/dialects/`). Lean 4 programs use `partial def` and `IO`. Rocq programs are pure `Fixpoint`s over an output monad defined in a small runtime, and are evaluated with `Eval vm_compute`. |\\n| Machine targets | NASM, CIL and JVM are written through a named stack machine and read back by lifting, so machine code translates to every language and between targets. |\\n| Modes | context-dependent (default, adapts comments such as C \\\"function call\\\" → C# \\\"method call\\\"), literal, same-effect |\\n| Extensibility | Every stage and rule list is an option of `createGrammarTranslator`; custom meta → meta layers are supported. |\\n| Common library | `common-library/` (output operations only, one file per language), enabled with `--common-library` |\\n\\n### Controlled natural languages\\n\\n- Data lives in `data/natural/*.lino`; `js/src/natural/` and `rust/src/natural/` read and write the same texts byte for byte.\\n- Covers the 30 most spoken languages (English, Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, Bengali, Portuguese, Russian, Urdu, Indonesian, German, Japanese, Marathi, Telugu, Turkish, Tamil, Vietnamese, Korean, Italian, Persian, Swahili, Tagalog, Thai, Poli

The source and the translation editors kept in step (issue 14): what is\n// selected on one side is selected on the other, the cursor and the scroll\n// follow, a part folded on one side is folded on the other, and the lines\n// that match are coloured alike (mapping.js) with a strip between the\n// editors joining them. The match is the `lineMap` of the translation\n// (line-map.js); without one (a natural language on one side) the editors\n// still scroll together, in proportion to their lengths.\n//\n// A change made here to the other editor must not come back: the cursor is\n// moved with the source 'api', which is not followed, scrolling and folding\n// done here are ignored while `applying` is set, and folding follows only\n// the regions whose state changed since the last look.\n\nimport { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';\nimport { lineLink } from './line-map.js';\nimport { connectorPaths, mappingDecorations } from './mapping.js';\nimport { debug } from './debug.js';\n\nconst foldingId = 'editor.contrib.folding';\n// monaco.editor.CursorChangeReason.ContentFlush: the text was replaced.\nconst contentFlush = 1;\n// After a text changes its folding regions are found again: folding is\n// not followed meanwhile.\nconst settleTime = 500;\n\nconst lineCount = (editor) => editor.getModel()?.getLineCount() ?? 0;\nconst clamp = (value, low, high) => Math.min(high, Math.max(low, value));\n\n// The height of line `line` (1-based) of an editor, as laid out.\nconst lineHeight = (editor, line) =>\n  Math.max(\n    editor.getBottomForLineNumber(line) - editor.getTopForLineNumber(line),\n    1\n  );\n\n// The line at the top of an editor, with the fraction of it scrolled past\n// (0-based: 2.5 is half way through the third line).\nexport function topPosition(editor) {\n  const count = lineCount(editor);\n  const scroll = editor.getScrollTop();\n  let low = 1;\n  let high = count;\n  while (low < high) {\n    const middle = (low + high + 1) >> 1;\n    if (editor.getTopForLineNumber(middle) <= scroll) {\n      low = middle;\n    } else {\n      high = middle - 1;\n    }\n  }\n  const top = editor.getTopForLineNumber(low);\n  const fraction = clamp((scroll - top) / lineHeight(editor, low), 0, 1);\n  return low - 1 + fraction;\n}\n\n// Scrolls an editor so that a position (as topPosition gives it) is at\n// its top.\nexport function scrollToPosition(editor, position) {\n  const count = lineCount(editor);\n  if (!count) {\n    return;\n  }\n  const at = clamp(position, 0, count);\n  const line = Math.min(count, Math.floor(at) + 1);\n  const fraction = at - (line - 1);\n  editor.setScrollTop(\n    editor.getTopForLineNumber(line) + fraction * lineHeight(editor, line)\n  );\n}\n\n// The lines [first, last] (0-based) of a selection; a selection that ends\n// at the start of a line does not take that line.\nfunction selectionLines(selection) {\n  const first = selection.startLineNumber - 1;\n  let last = selection.endLineNumber - 1;\n  if (last > first && selection.endColumn === 1) {\n    last -= 1;\n  }\n  return [first, last];\n}\n\n// The folded regions of an editor, by their first line (0-based).\nfunction foldedStarts(regions) {\n  const starts = new Set();\n  for (let index = 0; index < (regions?.length ?? 0); index += 1) {\n    if (regions.isCollapsed(index)) {\n      starts.add(regions.getStartLineNumber(index) - 1);\n    }\n  }\n  return starts;\n}\n\nasync function foldingModel(editor) {\n  try {\n    return (await editor.getContribution(foldingId)?.getFoldingModel()) ?? null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\n// The first region that starts in lines [first, last] (0-based).\nfunction regionStartingIn(regions, first, last) {\n  for (let index = 0; index < regions.length; index += 1) {\n    const start = regions.getStartLineNumber(index) - 1;\n    if (start >= first && start <= last) {\n      return index;\n    }\n  }\n  return -1;\n}\n\n// What changed between two sets of folded lines: [[line, folded], ...].\nfunction foldChanges(before, after) {\n  return [\n    ...[...after].filter((line) => !before.has(line)).map((l) => [l, true]),\n    ...[...before].filter((line) => !after.has(line)).map((l) => [l, false]),\n  ];\n}\n\n// The strip between the editors: a band per group of matched lines.\nfunction drawStrip(state) {\n  const { strip, editors, link, active } = state;\n  if (!strip?.isConnected) {\n    return;\n  }\n  const box = strip.getBoundingClientRect();\n  const span = (side, first, last) => {\n    const editor = editors[side];\n    const node = editor.getDomNode();\n    if (!node || last >= lineCount(editor)) {\n      return undefined;\n    }\n    const rect = node.getBoundingClientRect();\n    const offset = rect.top - box.top - editor.getScrollTop();\n    const top = offset + editor.getTopForLineNumber(first + 1);\n    const bottom = offset + editor.getBottomForLineNumber(last + 1);\n    const [low, high] = [rect.top - box.top, rect.bottom - box.top];\n    if (bottom <= low || top >= high) {\n      return undefined;\n    }\n    return { top: clamp(top, low, high), bottom: clamp(bottom, low, high) };\n  };\n  const paths = connectorPaths(link, span, box.width, active);\n  strip.setAttribute('viewBox', `0 0 ${box.width} ${box.height}`);\n  strip.innerHTML = paths\n    .map(\n      ({ colour, active: strong, d }) =>\n        `<path class=\"map-link map-c${colour}${strong ? ' map-active' : ''}\" d=\"${d}\"/>`\n    )\n    .join('');\n}\n\nfunction makeState(api, editors, strip) {\n  const state = {\n    api,\n    editors,\n    strip,\n    link: lineLink([], editors.map(lineCount)),\n    active: undefined,\n    applying: false,\n    settledAt: 0,\n    folded: [new Set(), new Set()],\n    collections: editors.map((editor) => editor.createDecorationsCollection()),\n    frame: 0,\n    disposed: false,\n  };\n  // Paints the colours of both editors and, at the next frame, the strip.\n  state.paint = () => {\n    state.collections.forEach((collection, side) => {\n      collection.set(\n        mappingDecorations(\n          state.link,\n          side,\n          state.active,\n          lineCount(editors[side])\n        )\n      );\n    });\n    state.redraw();\n  };\n  state.redraw = () => {\n    if (state.frame || state.disposed) {\n      return;\n    }\n    state.frame = globalThis.requestAnimationFrame(() => {\n      state.frame = 0;\n      if (!state.disposed) {\n        drawStrip(state);\n      }\n    });\n  };\n  return state;\n}\n\n// The cursor or the selection moved on one side: the same lines are\n// selected on the other side and the group under the cursor is coloured.\nfunction followSelection(state, side, event) {\n  if (\n    state.applying ||\n    event.source === 'api' ||\n    event.reason === contentFlush\n  ) {\n    return;\n  }\n  const { selection } = event;\n  const [first, last] = selectionLines(selection);\n  state.active = state.link.groupAt(side, selection.positionLineNumber - 1);\n  const other = state.editors[1 - side];\n  const count = lineCount(other);\n  if (count) {\n    const { lines } = state.link.mapRange(side, first, last);\n    const [from, to] = lines.map((line) => clamp(line, 0, count - 1) + 1);\n    const model = other.getModel();\n    state.applying = true;\n    try {\n      if (selection.isEmpty()) {\n        other.setPosition({\n          lineNumber: from,\n          column: model.getLineFirstNonWhitespaceColumn(from) || 1,\n        });\n      } else {\n        other.setSelection({\n          startLineNumber: from,\n          startColumn: 1,\n          endLineNumber: to,\n          endColumn: model.getLineMaxColumn(to),\n        });\n      }\n      other.revealLinesInCenterIfOutsideViewport(from, to);\n    } finally {\n      state.applying = false;\n    }\n  }\n  state.paint();\n}\n\n// One editor scrolled: the other scrolls to the matching line.\nfunction followScroll(state, side, event) {\n  state.redraw();\n  if (state.applying || !event.scrollTopChanged) {\n    return;\n  }\n  const position = state.link.mapPosition(\n    side,\n    topPosition(state.editors[side])\n  );\n  state.applying = true;\n  try {\n    scrollToPosition(state.editors[1 - side], position);\n  } finally {\n    state.applying = false;\n  }\n}\n\n// Regions were folded or unfolded on one side: the matching regions on\n// the other side follow.\nasync function followFolding(state, side) {\n  const quiet = state.applying || Date.now() < state.settledAt;\n  const model = await foldingModel(state.editors[side]);\n  const after = foldedStarts(model?.regions);\n  const changes = foldChanges(state.folded[side], after);\n  state.folded[side] = after;\n  state.redraw();\n  if (quiet || state.disposed || !changes.length) {\n    return;\n  }\n  const other = await foldingModel(state.editors[1 - side]);\n  if (!other || state.disposed) {\n    return;\n  }\n  const { regions } = other;\n  const toggled = new Map();\n  for (const [line, folded] of changes) {\n    const { lines } = state.link.mapRange(side, line);\n    const index = regionStartingIn(regions, ...lines);\n    if (index >= 0 && regions.isCollapsed(index) !== folded) {\n      toggled.set(index, regions.toRegion(index));\n    }\n  }\n  debug('sync', 'folding', side, changes, [...toggled.keys()]);\n  if (toggled.size) {\n    state.applying = true;\n    try {\n      other.toggleCollapseState([...toggled.values()]);\n    } finally {\n      state.applying = false;\n    }\n  }\n  state.folded[1 - side] = foldedStarts(other.regions);\n}\n\n// After a text changed, the folded regions are looked at again before\n// folding is followed.\nfunction settle(state) {\n  state.settledAt = Date.now() + settleTime;\n  globalThis.clearTimeout(state.settleTimer);\n  state.settleTimer = globalThis.setTimeout(async () => {\n    const models = await Promise.all(state.editors.map(foldingModel));\n    models.forEach((model, side) => {\n      state.folded[side] = foldedStarts(model?.regions);\n    });\n    state.redraw();\n  }, settleTime + 100);\n}\n\n// Links two Monaco editors ([source, target]); `strip` is the <svg>\n// between them, if any. update(lineMap) is called whenever either text or\n// the translation changes.\nexport function linkEditors(api, editors, strip) {\n  const state = makeState(api, editors, strip);\n  const subscriptions = editors.flatMap((editor, side) => [\n    editor.onDidChangeCursorSelection((event) =>\n      followSelection(state, side, event)\n    ),\n    editor.onDidScrollChange((event) => followScroll(state, side, event)),\n    editor.onDidChangeHiddenAreas(() => followFolding(state, side)),\n    editor.onDidChangeModelContent(() => settle(state)),\n    editor.onDidLayoutChange(() => state.redraw()),\n    editor.onDidContentSizeChange(() => state.redraw()),\n  ]);\n  const resize = () => state.redraw();\n  globalThis.addEventListener?.('resize', resize);\n  return {\n    update(lineMap) {\n      state.link = lineLink(lineMap, editors.map(lineCount));\n      const position = editors[0].getPosition();\n      state.active =\n        position && editors[0].hasTextFocus()\n          ? state.link.groupAt(0, position.lineNumber - 1)\n          : undefined;\n      debug('sync', 'line map', lineMap, state.link.groups.length);\n      state.paint();\n    },\n    dispose() {\n      state.disposed = true;\n      globalThis.cancelAnimationFrame(state.frame);\n      globalThis.clearTimeout(state.settleTimer);\n      globalThis.removeEventListener?.('resize', resize);\n      subscriptions.forEach((it) => it.dispose());\n      for (const collection of state.collections) {\n        try {\n          collection.clear();\n        } catch {\n          // The editor is gone already.\n        }\n      }\n      if (strip) {\n        strip.innerHTML = '';\n      }\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n// The React side: `panes` are [source, target] as CodeEditor's onMount\n// gives them ({ editor, api } or undefined); the link is made when both\n// are there and follows `lineMap` and the texts (whose line counts it\n// needs).\nexport function useEditorSync(panes, strip, lineMap, source, target) {\n  const [sourcePane, targetPane] = panes;\n  const link = useRef();\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!sourcePane || !targetPane) {\n      return undefined;\n    }\n    const linked = linkEditors(\n      sourcePane.api,\n      [sourcePane.editor, targetPane.editor],\n      strip.current\n    );\n    link.current = linked;\n    return () => {\n      linked.dispose();\n      link.current = undefined;\n    };\n  }, [sourcePane, targetPane, strip]);\n  useEffect(() => {\n    link.current?.update(lineMap);\n  }, [sourcePane, targetPane, lineMap, source, target]);\n}\n// A text pane: the source (editable), the translation, the meta views and\n// the rules. The Monaco editor (the default) is loaded the first time it is\n// needed; the plain editor, a choice in the settings, is a textarea or a\n// coloured <pre>.\n// Both colour words the same way (highlight.js) and wrap long lines or not\n// (the word-wrap setting).\n\nimport {\n  createElement as h,\n  useEffect,\n  useMemo,\n  useRef,\n  useState,\n} from 'react';\nimport { highlightText, pieces } from './highlight.js';\nimport { debug } from './debug.js';\n\n// The coloured lines of a read-only plain pane.\nfunction Coloured({ text, lexicon }) {\n  const lines = useMemo(() => {\n    const all = text.split('\\n');\n    return highlightText(text, lexicon).map((tokens, index) =>\n      pieces(all[index], tokens)\n    );\n  }, [text, lexicon]);\n  return lines.map((parts, index) =>\n    h(\n      'span',\n      { key: index, className: 'line' },\n      parts.map(([part, type], at) =>\n        type ? h('span', { key: at, className: `hl-${type}` }, part) : part\n      ),\n      index < lines.length - 1 ? '\\n' : null\n    )\n  );\n}\n\nfunction PlainEditor({ id, value, onChange, readOnly, lexicon, className }) {\n  if (!readOnly) {\n    return h('textarea', {\n      id,\n      className,\n      spellCheck: false,\n      value,\n      onChange: (event) => onChange(event.target.value),\n    });\n  }\n  return h(\n    'pre',\n    { id, className },\n    lexicon ? h(Coloured, { text: value, lexicon }) : value\n  );\n}\n\nlet panes = 0;\n\n// The colours and the folding regions of a pane, set again when its\n// lexicon changes.\nfunction paneFeatures(api, module, language, lexicon) {\n  const features = [\n    module.colourPane(api, language, lexicon),\n    module.foldPane(api, language, lexicon),\n  ];\n  return { dispose: () => features.forEach((it) => it.dispose()) };\n}\n\n// The Monaco pane grows with its text, between the height of the plain\n// panes and 70% of the window; the pane beside it stretches to match.\n// onMount({ editor, api }) is called when the editor is made, and\n// onMount(undefined) when it is gone (editor-sync.js links two panes).\nfunction MonacoEditor({\n  id,\n  value,\n  onChange,\n  onMount,\n  readOnly,\n  lexicon,\n  wrap,\n  label,\n}) {\n  const holder = useRef();\n  const editor = useRef();\n  const monaco = useRef();\n  const language = useRef(`universal-translator-${(panes += 1)}`);\n  const latest = useRef({ value, onChange, onMount, lexicon });\n  latest.current = { value, onChange, onMount, lexicon };\n  const [failed, setFailed] = useState('');\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    let disposed = false;\n    let cleanup = () => {};\n    import('./monaco.js')\n      .then(async (module) => {\n        const api = await module.loadMonaco();\n        if (disposed) {\n          return;\n        }\n        debug('monaco', 'loaded for', id);\n        monaco.current = { api, module };\n        // The lexicon of now: the text may have changed while loading.\n        const provider = paneFeatures(\n          api,\n          module,\n          language.current,\n          latest.current.lexicon\n        );\n        module.applySkin(api);\n        const instance = api.editor.create(holder.current, {\n          value: latest.current.value,\n          language: language.current,\n          readOnly,\n          ariaLabel: label,\n          automaticLayout: true,\n          minimap: { enabled: false },\n          scrollBeyondLastLine: false,\n          wordWrap: wrap ? 'on' : 'off',\n          fontSize: 14,\n          lineNumbersMinChars: 3,\n          renderLineHighlight: readOnly ? 'none' : 'line',\n          scrollbar: { alwaysConsumeMouseWheel: false },\n          folding: true,\n          showFoldingControls: 'always',\n        });\n        editor.current = instance;\n        const fit = () => {\n          const most = globalThis.innerHeight * 0.7;\n          holder.current.style.minHeight = `${Math.min(\n            most,\n            Math.max(260, instance.getContentHeight())\n          )}px`;\n        };\n        fit();\n        const subscriptions = [\n          instance.onDidContentSizeChange(fit),\n          instance.onDidChangeModelContent(() => {\n            const text = instance.getValue();\n            if (text !== latest.current.value) {\n              latest.current.onChange?.(text);\n            }\n          }),\n        ];\n        // The skin or the scheme changed: colour the editors anew.\n        const repaint = () => module.applySkin(api);\n        const observer = new globalThis.MutationObserver(repaint);\n        observer.observe(globalThis.document.documentElement, {\n          attributes: true,\n          attributeFilter: ['data-theme', 'data-scheme', 'data-contrast'],\n        });\n        // Only the skin's stylesheet (settings.js) counts: Monaco writes\n        // styles of its own to <head> when its theme is set.\n        const skinChanged = (mutations) =>\n          mutations.some(({ target, addedNodes, removedNodes }) =>\n            [target, ...addedNodes, ...removedNodes].some(\n              (node) => node.id === 'ui-theme'\n            )\n          );\n        const styleObserver = new globalThis.MutationObserver((mutations) => {\n          if (skinChanged(mutations)) {\n            repaint();\n          }\n        });\n        styleObserver.observe(globalThis.document.head, {\n          childList: true,\n          subtree: true,\n        });\n        const media = globalThis.matchMedia?.('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)');\n        media?.addEventListener('change', repaint);\n        latest.current.onMount?.({ editor: instance, api });\n        cleanup = () => {\n          latest.current.onMount?.(undefined);\n          provider.dispose();\n          subscriptions.forEach((it) => it.dispose());\n          observer.disconnect();\n          styleObserver.disconnect();\n          media?.removeEventListener('change', repaint);\n          instance.getModel()?.dispose();\n          instance.dispose();\n        };\n      })\n      .catch((error) => {\n        debug('monaco', 'failed', error);\n        setFailed(error.message);\n      });\n    return () => {\n      disposed = true;\n      cleanup();\n    };\n    // The editor is made once; its text and options follow below.\n  }, []);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const instance = editor.current;\n    if (instance && instance.getValue() !== value) {\n      instance.setValue(value);\n    }\n  }, [value]);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    editor.current?.updateOptions({ wordWrap: wrap ? 'on' : 'off', readOnly });\n  }, [wrap, readOnly]);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (monaco.current) {\n      const { api, module } = monaco.current;\n      const provider = paneFeatures(api, module, language.current, lexicon);\n      return () => provider.dispose();\n    }\n    return undefined;\n  }, [lexicon]);\n\n  if (failed) {\n    return h(PlainEditor, { id, value, onChange, readOnly, lexicon });\n  }\n  return h('div', {\n    id,\n    ref: holder,\n    className: 'code-editor monaco',\n    'data-editor': 'monaco',\n    'data-value': value,\n  });\n}\n\n// engine: 'monaco' (the default) or 'plain'.\nexport function CodeEditor({ engine = 'monaco', ...props }) {\n  return engine === 'plain' ? h(PlainEditor, props) : h(MonacoEditor, props);\n}\n// How the match between the lines of both editors is shown (issue 14), as\n// in diff tools and Compiler Explorer:\n//\n// - every group of matched lines has a background colour of a cycling\n//   palette, the same in both editors, and a bar of that colour beside its\n//   line numbers;\n// - the group under the cursor (in either editor) is coloured stronger;\n// - a strip between the editors joins the lines of each group on the left\n//   to its lines on the right.\n//\n// The colours are CSS classes (styles.css: map-line, map-c0 … map-c5,\n// map-active). Nothing here needs Monaco: editor-sync.js gives the\n// decorations to the editors and the paths to the strip.\n\n// Monaco decorations for one side (0 the source, 1 the target) of a link\n// (line-map.js); `active` is the group under the cursor, if any.\nexport function mappingDecorations(link, side, active, lineCount = Infinity) {\n  const decorations = [];\n  for (const group of link.groups) {\n    const colour = `map-c${group.colour}`;\n    const strong = group === active ? ' map-active' : '';\n    for (const line of group.lines[side]) {\n      if (line >= lineCount) {\n        continue;\n      }\n      decorations.push({\n        range: {\n          startLineNumber: line + 1,\n          startColumn: 1,\n          endLineNumber: line + 1,\n          endColumn: 1,\n        },\n        options: {\n          isWholeLine: true,\n          className: `map-line ${colour}${strong}`,\n          linesDecorationsClassName: `map-gutter ${colour}${strong}`,\n        },\n      });\n    }\n  }\n  return decorations;\n}\n\n// The lines of a group on one side that are next to each other.\nfunction runs(lines) {\n  const all = [];\n  for (const line of lines) {\n    const last = all.at(-1);\n    if (last && line === last[1] + 1) {\n      last[1] = line;\n    } else {\n      all.push([line, line]);\n    }\n  }\n  return all;\n}\n\n// The shapes of the strip between the editors, `width` wide. `span(side,\n// first, last)` gives where lines first … last of a side are in the strip,\n// as { top, bottom } clipped to the editor, or undefined when they cannot\n// be seen. A group of lines on both sides is one band per run of lines.\nexport function connectorPaths(link, span, width, active) {\n  const middle = width / 2;\n  const paths = [];\n  for (const group of link.groups) {\n    const [left, right] = group.lines.map(runs);\n    const count = Math.max(left.length, right.length);\n    for (let at = 0; at < count; at += 1) {\n      const from = left[Math.min(at, left.length - 1)];\n      const to = right[Math.min(at, right.length - 1)];\n      const a = span(0, ...from);\n      const b = span(1, ...to);\n      if (!a || !b) {\n        continue;\n      }\n      paths.push({\n        colour: group.colour,\n        active: group === active,\n        d: [\n          `M0 ${a.top}`,\n          `C${middle} ${a.top} ${middle} ${b.top} ${width} ${b.top}`,\n          `L${width} ${b.bottom}`,\n          `C${middle} ${b.bottom} ${middle} ${a.bottom} 0 ${a.bottom}`,\n          'Z',\n        ].join(' '),\n      });\n    }\n  }\n  return paths;\n}\n// The lines of a source and of its translation matched to each other, for\n// the two editors of the Translate tab (issue 14). The translator returns\n// the match as `lineMap`: pairs of 0-based [source line, target line] (see\n// js/src/translation/layout.js). From it a link between both texts gives:\n//\n// - groups: lines that belong together (a statement written on three lines\n//   on one side and on one on the other), each with a colour of a cycling\n//   palette, so both editors show what translates to what;\n// - ranges: the lines on the other side of a selection;\n// - positions: where to scroll the other editor to. Lines matched exactly\n//   are anchors; between two anchors a position moves in proportion, so a\n//   part that takes ten lines on one side and two on the other scrolls\n//   both editors through it together, as diff tools do.\n//\n// Nothing here needs Monaco or React: editor-sync.js applies it to the\n// editors. A side is 0 (the source) or 1 (the target).\n\nexport const paletteSize = 6;\n\n// Connected pairs: a line on either side joins every pair it is part of.\nfunction components(pairs) {\n  const parent = new Map();\n  const find = (key) => {\n    let root = key;\n    while (parent.get(root) !== root) {\n      root = parent.get(root);\n    }\n    parent.set(key, root);\n    return root;\n  };\n  const join = (a, b) => {\n    for (const key of [a, b]) {\n      if (!parent.has(key)) {\n        parent.set(key, key);\n      }\n    }\n    parent.set(find(a), find(b));\n  };\n  for (const [source, target] of pairs) {\n    join(`s${source}`, `t${target}`);\n  }\n  const groups = new Map();\n  for (const [source, target] of pairs) {\n    const root = find(`s${source}`);\n    if (!groups.has(root)) {\n      groups.set(root, [new Set(), new Set()]);\n    }\n    groups.get(root)[0].add(source);\n    groups.get(root)[1].add(target);\n  }\n  return [...groups.values()].map((sides) =>\n    sides.map((lines) => [...lines].sort((a, b) => a - b))\n  );\n}\n\n// The longest chain of pairs that goes down on both sides at once: the\n// anchors of scrolling (a pair that crosses another is left out).\nfunction monotonicChain(pairs) {\n  const sorted = [...pairs].sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0] || b[1] - a[1]);\n  const tails = [];\n  const previous = [];\n  sorted.forEach(([, target], index) => {\n    let low = 0;\n    let high = tails.length;\n    while (low < high) {\n      const middle = (low + high) >> 1;\n      if (sorted[tails[middle]][1] < target) {\n        low = middle + 1;\n      } else {\n        high = middle;\n      }\n    }\n    // A later pair on the same target line keeps the earlier anchor: a\n    // part of several source lines scrolls from its first line on.\n    if (low < tails.length && sorted[tails[low]][1] === target) {\n      return;\n    }\n    previous[index] = low > 0 ? tails[low - 1] : -1;\n    tails[low] = index;\n  });\n  // Equal source lines come with the larger target first, so the chain\n  // has one anchor per line on both sides.\n  const chain = [];\n  for (let at = tails.at(-1) ?? fill(language, 'array', {\n            elements: separated(expression.elements, language),\n          })\n        : fill(language, 'new-array', {\n            length: [{ type: 'number', value: 0 }],\n            fill: [{ type: 'number', value: 0 }],\n          });\n    case 'NewArray':\n      return fill(language, 'new-array', {\n        length: operand(expression.length, language),\n        fill: operand(expression.fill, language),\n      });\n    case 'Index':\n      return fill(language, 'element', {\n        index: operand(expression.index, language),\n        array: operand(expression.array, language),\n      });\n    case 'Length':\n      return fill(language, 'length', {\n        array: operand(expression.array, language),\n      });\n    default:\n      throw new Error(`Cannot write a ${expression.kind} expression in words`);\n  }\n}\n\n// Tokens of an expression that must bind at least as tightly as `minimum`.\nexport function writeExpression(expression, language, minimum = 0) {\n  const level = levelOf(expression);\n  let tokens;\n  if (expression.kind === 'Interpolation') {\n    tokens = expression.parts\n      .map((part) => writeExpression(part, language, level + 1))\n      .reduce((left, right) => fill(language, 'join', { left, right }));\n  } else if (expression.kind === 'Binary') {\n    tokens = fill(\n      language,\n      binaryTemplates[expression.operator],\n      binarySlots(expression, language, level)\n    );\n  } else if (expression.kind === 'Unary') {\n    tokens = fill(language, unaryTemplates[expression.operator], {\n      operand: writeExpression(expression.operand, language, level),\n    });\n  } else {\n    tokens = primary(expression, language);\n  }\n  return level < minimum ? parenthesize(tokens) : tokens;\n}\n\n// Tokens -> text. Spaces go between tokens, except next to parentheses and\n// before separators.\nexport function renderTokens(tokens, language) {\n  const [opening, closing] = language.quotes;\n  let output = '';\n  let previous;\n  for (const token of tokens) {\n    const text =\n      token.type =[REDACTED] 'text'\n        ? `${opening}${token.value.split(closing).join(closing + closing)}${closing}`\n        : String(token.value);\n    const glued =\n      !previous ||\n      previous.type === 'open' ||\n      token.type =[REDACTED] 'close' ||\n      token.type =[REDACTED] 'separator';\n    output += glued ? text : ` ${text}`;\n    previous = token;\n  }\n  return output;\n}\n\nfunction capitalize(sentence) {\n  return sentence.charAt(0).toLocaleUpperCase() + sentence.slice(1);\n}\n\nclass Writer {\n  constructor(language) {\n    this.language = language;\n    this.lines = [];\n  }\n\n  sentence(depth, key, slots, opensBlock = false) {\n    const { language } = this;\n    const text = renderTokens(fill(language, key, slots), language);\n    const end = opensBlock ? language.blockEnd : language.sentenceEnd;\n    this.lines.push(`${indentUnit.repeat(depth)}${capitalize(text)}${end}`);\n  }\n\n  // A comment of several lines becomes one note per line.\n  note(depth, text) {\n    for (const part of text.split('\\n')) {\n      const line = this.language.note.replace('{text}', part.trim());\n      this.lines.push(`${indentUnit.repeat(depth)}${line}`);\n    }\n  }\n\n  expression(value, level = 0) {\n    return writeExpression(value, this.language, level);\n  }\n\n  block(block, depth) {\n    const statements = block?.statements ?? [];\n    if (!statements.length) {\n      this.sentence(depth, 'nothing', {});\n    }\ngrammar:\n  english:\n    infinitive: 'to {verb}'\n    verb-forms: lemma present\n    endings: 's' 'es' 'ed' 'ing'\n  french:\n    verb-lemma: infinitive\n    verb-forms: lemma present\n    endings: 's' 'x' 'e' 'es' 'er' 'ez' 'ent' 'ons' 'é' 'ée' 'és'\n  polish:\n    verb-lemma: infinitive\n    verb-forms: A node of one\ngrammar keeps its text and gains a `reading` in another grammar:\n\n| Host       | Nested reading                    | Example                                   |\n| ---------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |\n| comment    | `Prose > Sentence > Word`         | `// Prints the sum`                       |\n| prose      | `Code` (any programming language) | `` // Prints `x + 1` ``                   |\n| string     | `Code` when it reads as code      | `code = \"print(1 + 2)\"`                   |\n| string     | `Prose` otherwise                 | `\"Привет мир\"`                            |\n| long texts | `Paragraph` under `texts`, by id  | a comment and a string with the same text |\n\nReadings are additions. An emitter that does not know them ignores them, and\n`unnest` returns the plain program. New host or nested languages therefore\nneed no change to the emitters. A new grammar becomes nestable as soon as\n`parseFragment` reads it.\n\n### Natural language\n\nThe design follows GF (`prior-art.md` section 3.1):\n\n- **abstract syntax**: concepts. Words in `data/natural/vocabulary.lino` and\n  sentence templates in `data/natural/<language>.lino` are keyed by concept\n  ids such as `hello`, `print` and `if`;\n- **concrete syntax**: one description per language. Templates read and\n  write whole algorithm sentences. The prose reader\n  (`natural/prose-reading`) reads any other text into words, each with its\n  concept and part of speech;\n- **lexical choice**: the first word of a concept is the most frequent one.\n  Translation picks it unless the source used a word that survives the round\n  trip (`prior-art.md` section 3.9).\n\nNew depth is added in the same tree, so nothing is rewritten:\n\n- morphology (UniMorph features) goes on `Word`;\n- dependencies (Universal Dependencies or Link Grammar links) are links\n  between the `Word`s of a `Sentence`.\n\nThe spaCy, Stanza and NLTK pipelines (tokenize, tag, parse) correspond to the\nreader stages. We do not use them at run time: their models are large and\nwritten in Python, and the translator must run in a browser.\n\n### Targets beyond source languages\n\nMachine targets (NASM, CIL, JVM) use the same meta program, lowered first\n(`formal/lowering`). They can be read back (`formal/machine-reader`, lifting).\nAssembly dialects and other intermediate languages are a syntax table over a\nshared instruction model, as `prior-art.md` section 5.3 recommends. The\nscores are truth values in the style of relative-meta-logic: numbers in\n[0, 1] on a grid of six decimals, combined by their product\n(`js/src/natural/probability.js`; the Rust twin uses the package's\n`TruthValue` and `Aggregator::Product`).\n\n- **Frequency.** A phrase's meanings are listed most frequent first. Each\n  one gets a Zipf prior, 1 / rank normalized to sum 1 (two meanings:\n  0.666667 and 0.333333). The frequency of a translation is the product of\n  the priors of the readings it takes.\n- **Round trip.** The meanings of the translation are read back in the\n  target language and compared with the meanings of the source: the longest\n  common subsequence of the two lists over the longer length.\n- **Coverage.** The share of lines translated, 1 when the translation is\n  complete.\n- **Probability.** frequency × round trip × coverage.\n\nThe choices are in prose: comments, declared names, and the sentences of a\nnatural language that no template reads. Code is translated one way by its\nrules. `rankProse` (`rank_prose`) searches the readings of one prose part\ngreedily. It starts from the most frequent reading of every phrase and\ntries the other readings of one phrase at a time. A reading is kept only\nwhen the probability gets strictly higher. At most 16 translations are\nscored. So the default translation changes only when another reading\nsurvives the round trip strictly better.\n\n`translateCandidates` (`Translator::translate_candidates`) ranks every prose\npart of a text. Its first candidate is the text `translatePartial` writes.\nEach other candidate takes one other translation of one part. A translator\nthat has its own comment translator gives a single candidate. On the\ncommand line, `translate <from> <to> --candidates` prints one candidate per\nline:\n\n```text\n$ printf 'Привет мир. Как дела?' | universal-translator translate russian english - --candidates\n(text 'Hello world. How do?\n') (probability 0.296297) (frequency 0.296297) (roundTrip 1) (coverage 1)\n(text 'Hello peace. How do?\n') (probability 0.111111) (frequency 0.148148) (roundTrip 0.75) (coverage 1)\n(text 'Hello world. Like do?\n') (probability 0.111111) (frequency 0.148148) (roundTrip 0.75) (coverage 1)\n(text 'Hello world. How to make?\n') (probability 0.111111) (frequency 0.148148) (roundTrip 0.75) (coverage 1)\n```\n\nThe meta program records what a reading loses (`js/src/meta/imprecision.js`\nand `js/src/natural/prose-reading.js`) as attributes of the node:\n\n| Kind                         | Where                                                              | Attributes                                                               |\n| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `(imprecision ambiguous)`    | a word of prose with more than one meaning                         | `(alternatives n)`, and `(probability p)`, the prior of the reading kept |\n| `(imprecision untranslated)` | a word of prose with no known meaning; a translation keeps it      |                                                                          |\n| `(imprecision truncated)`    | a number with a fraction, typed as an integer                      |                                                                          |\n| `(imprecision rounded)`      | an integer beyond 2^53 − 1, the largest one a double keeps exactly |                                                                          |\n\n`meta` prints these attributes, in Links Notation and with `--json`.\nEmitters ignore them: `imprecision` is one of the keys that the essence of\na node leaves out, and `alternatives` and `probability` are only set on\nwords of a prose reading, which no emitter writes.\n\nLimits:\n\n- In a long text with many ambiguous words, the frequency product falls\n  towards 0. Every candidate is then close to 0, and the default is kept.\n- Only prose is ranked. The structure of code, and the templates of the\n  controlled languages, have one reading each.\n- A run of letters inside one word of a language written without spaces\n  shares one reading key with the same run elsewhere in that word.\n- `truncated` is recorded only while type inference calls a number with a\n  fraction an integer.\n# Prior art for issue 14\n\nResearch date: 2026-11-25.
